statements.text: A property is absolutely intrinsic to a thing when it is intrinsic and not necessitated by purely extrinsic properties of the thing’s parts. A comparatively intrinsic property, such as a sphere’s shape, is intrinsic but necessitated by such extrinsic properties.

sources.quote: P is an absolutely intrinsic property of X just in case P is an intrinsic property of X, and P is not necessitated by purely extrinsic properties of parts of X.
relatively intrinsic properties are intrinsic properties that are nothing over and above extrinsic properties
